title: Time-Bound Quantitative Drills
tagline: Year 4 — Short, fast questions with a target time per question, and a method for pacing a timed section

introduction.overview: A timed section is a budget of seconds. If you have 30 questions in 40 minutes, you have 80 seconds per question on average, but they are not equal: easy ones should take 30–45 seconds, hard ones may deserve 2 minutes or a skip. This chapter practises fast, simple questions and a pacing method: set a target time per question type, check progress at fixed points and decide quickly when to skip.
introduction.placementRelevance: Online assessments are timed and sectional; speed with accuracy decides the score.
introduction.realWorldContext: Working to deadlines and splitting time across tasks is the same discipline.

learningObjectives: Compute the average time per question
Set checkpoints during a timed section
Answer easy questions in under 45 seconds
Estimate scores from attempts and accuracy

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Time per question = total time ÷ questions. Accuracy = correct ÷ attempted.

coreDefinitions: Pace: the average time you spend per question.
Checkpoint: a planned moment to compare progress with plan.
Skip: leaving a question to return later.
Drill: a short timed practice set.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: You are paid in marks, and each second spent on a hard question is a second not spent on an easy one.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Fix your average, set checkpoints at quarter marks, and move on after about twice the average time.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Checkpoint
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Questions done by time t = t ÷ pace

mainNarrative: A section of 30 questions in 40 minutes gives 2,400 seconds, so 80 seconds on average. Plan 40 s for easy, 80 s for medium and skip anything that passes about 160 s.
Use checkpoints: after 10 minutes you should have worked through about 7–8 questions.
If you attempt 28 questions and 24 are right, accuracy is 24 ÷ 28 = 85.7%.
With 1 mark for each right answer and a quarter-mark penalty for each wrong one, 24 right and 4 wrong score 24 − 1 = 23.
Easy questions (percentage of a number, simple ratios) should take under 40 seconds; practise until they do.

deepDiveAspects.title: Sunk-cost trap
deepDiveAspects.content: Do not keep working a question only because you have already spent time on it.

deepDiveAspects.title: Two passes
deepDiveAspects.content: Pass 1: all questions solvable in under a minute. Pass 2: the rest, easiest first.

solvedExamples.title: Pace
solvedExamples.question: A section has 30 questions in 40 minutes. What is the average time per question?

solvedExamples.title: Accuracy
solvedExamples.question: You attempt 28 questions and 24 are correct. Accuracy?

solvedExamples.title: Score
solvedExamples.question: 24 correct, 4 wrong, 1 mark each right and ¼ mark penalty each wrong. Score?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Know your pace, check progress at quarter marks, and skip once a question passes about twice the pace.

commonMistakes.mistake: Spending equal time on all questions

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate two options quickly rather than solving fully.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Do a timed drill every day.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Speed is built by easy questions done fast.
